body.estimand_functional: \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\tau_R)=(\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B,\ q^\top\{\widehat s_1-\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B\})\), with root-\(K\) influence \((\Phi_{\theta},\Phi_\tau)\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed set of target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and target factual-post cells is observed; treatment histories and grid times are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each cell contains \(K\) independent individuals, and cell samples are mutually independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The target switches treatment after the pre period, while donor units remain under control; exact donor-span transport identifies the target's untreated post-period survival row.
sampling_model.overlap: Conditional censor survival is at least \(g>0\) through every required cell horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates the conditional event and censor survival functions with rates \(a_K\) and \(b_K\) satisfying \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 identify the donor-span counterfactual and give finite-sample consistency for Kaplan--Meier spectral SSC under non-informative censoring.
Theorem 2 gives pointwise and uniform asymptotic linearity for one cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

body.tldr: A fixed survival panel can be made robust to covariate-dependent right censoring by replacing every Kaplan--Meier cell curve with one cross-fitted augmented-IPCW score and transporting the resulting joint influence vector through the complete rank-\(r\) pseudoinverse derivative. The resulting estimator has a joint root-\(K\) Gaussian law, a feasible simultaneous band for the untreated post-treatment curve, and a studentized grid-RMST effect interval. A complementary probability-limit result derives the unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR pseudo-target and proves fixed nonzero bias on a relatively open subclass containing an explicit rational law.

project_justification.gap: Synthetic Survival Control identifies a clinically relevant low-rank counterfactual but assumes non-informative censoring and provides no influence-function limit law, while modern orthogonal survival estimators stop before the learned panel map.
project_justification.niche: With fixed panel dimensions and many independent patients per cell, the cellwise survival problem is semiparametric but the final counterfactual is a smooth, multi-block spectral functional whose full derivative and covariance have not been developed.
project_justification.fill: The project fixes the score and tie convention, proves its joint product-rate expansion, derives the complete transported influence vector, validates multiplier and grid-RMST inference, and derives the unadjusted workflow's probability limit with an explicit relatively open nonzero-bias subclass.

body.related_work: Han and Shah (2025) supply the low-rank survival-panel estimand, donor transport, and TCL application, but their Kaplan--Meier theory assumes non-informative censoring and explicitly points to IPCW as future work. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024) supply the score and product-integral remainder argument adapted here at the cell level, but do not estimate a donor map. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025) clarify minimum-norm PCR and row-space transport, without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973) supply the constant-rank pseudoinverse differential used as a technique ancestor. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024) motivate the failure analysis by showing distinct distributional biases in survival synthetic controls, but do not derive the cellwise informative-censoring PCR pseudo-limit or its relatively open nonzero-bias region. Fan and Liao (2022, Theorem 2.1 and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1; arXiv v3, pp. 10--11 and 20--21) use cross-sectional diversified projections to recover factor spaces and validate factor-augmented inference with weak or over-estimated factors as the cross-sectional dimension grows. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) obtain rank-robust inference for high-dimensional linear functionals. Those high-dimensional factor methods inform the stabilization handle but do not resolve a fixed-panel nonlinear pseudoinverse at a local singular collision.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theorem is deliberately fixed-dimensional. It does not cover a growing post grid, a shrinking singular gap, a selected rank, covariance degeneracy, or a continuous-time RMST. The grid-RMST target is exactly \(q^\top(s_1-\theta)\); calling it a continuous restricted mean would require an additional observation or interpolation model.
body.honest_scope: The cellwise second-order remainder and plug-in influence consistency are the early kill test. Once that lemma is established, constant-rank differentiation and fixed-dimensional Gaussian calibration are standard but must retain all cell blocks. Under marginal independent censoring with correctly estimated constant nuisances, the augmented-IPCW cell influence reduces to the ordinary Kaplan--Meier influence, providing the required reduction to Han and Shah's regular special case. The weak-gap/rank-selection frontier remains an explicit open-ended question rather than an asserted rate.
